advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Update the run_git docstring to say str stdin is encoded as UTF-8 by run_git, sent as exact bytes, and the output decoded with universal newlines
evidence: src/rebar/_store/gitutil.py:182-183: ``input_data`` (when set) is fed to git's stdin — forwarded to :func:`subprocess.run`'s ``input``
src/rebar/_store/gitutil.py:185-186: with ``text=True`` (the default), ``input_data`` must be ``str`` — :func:`subprocess.run` encodes text-mode stdin.
src/rebar/_store/gitutil.py:196-205: str input with text=True now routes to _run_with_text_stdin
advisory.finding: The run_git docstring still says str input_data is forwarded to subprocess.run's input and that subprocess.run encodes text-mode stdin. Neither is true any more: str stdin is now encoded by run_git itself and git runs in binary mode, with output decoded afterwards.
scenarios: A maintainer reads the run_git contract and assumes platform newline translation still applies to str stdin.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] In test_the_bounded_path_also_sends_bytes, assert out.stdout equals git's hash of the exact bytes b"a\nb\n" (as the non-bounded test does), not just a 40-character length.
evidence: The SpyPopen records only constructor kwargs; the stdin payload goes to `proc.communicate(input, ...)` (src/rebar/_store/gitutil.py:309), which the test never captures or checks.
The non-bounded sibling test does pin the exact output: `assert out.stdout == expected`, where expected is git's hash of b"a\nb\n".
src/rebar/_store/gitutil.py:282: `def _run_in_group(` is a private helper inside the unit under test.
The other new tests in the same file fake the external boundary instead (`gitutil.subprocess.run` / `gitutil.subprocess.Popen`).
advisory.finding: The bounded-path test never checks the bytes fed to git's stdin or the resulting hash. It asserts only that Popen got `text=False` and that the hash is 40 characters long, so it would stay green if the bounded path encoded the text wrongly (for example by putting `\r\n` back or using another codec).
merged_from: test_a_timeout_carries_decoded_text replaces the private helper `gitutil._run_in_group` instead of faking the subprocess boundary. Renaming or inlining that internal helper without changing behaviour would break the test.
scenarios: A future change to `_run_with_text_stdin` or `_run_in_group` sends CRLF or wrongly encoded bytes on the timeout path, which is the Windows bug this diff fixes, and the test still passes because any SHA-1 hex is 40 characters.
advisory.suggested_fix: Compute `expected = subprocess.run(["git", "-C", str(repo), "hash-object", "--stdin"], input=b"a\nb\n", capture_output=True).stdout.decode()` with the real subprocess.run before patching, then `assert out.stdout == expected`.

dropped.finding: _run_with_text_stdin calls back into run_git through the module-level name gitutil.run_git, which tests can patch. A test spy that wraps gitutil.run_git is hit twice for every str-stdin call: once with text=True and str input, then again with text=False and bytes input. A spy that returns a fake text-mode result (str stdout) for matching args would make _decode_git_text call .decode on a str and crash.
scenarios: A spy that counts or asserts on run_git calls sees duplicate entries for callers that pass str input_data.
A partial fake that returns CompletedProcess(..., stdout=str) for some args crashes with AttributeError: 'str' object has no attribute 'decode' when the caller passed str stdin.
dropped.suggested_fix: Move the argv/_run_in_group/subprocess.run body of run_git into a private _run_git_raw(...) helper. run_git and _run_with_text_stdin both call it, so the binary re-entry never goes through the public, monkeypatchable run_git name.
